zh.summary: SOLISTIQ 以自研基础模型 Q-Foundry 为内核，面向工业与商业企业提供从需求预测到自动补货建议的 AI 库存决策闭环。
zh.judgment: 把库存优化从逐条规则引擎升级为单一预训练基础模型，若 24% 降误差与 15–25% 降库存的公司披露数据在客户侧得到验证，将直接切中制造与贸易企业最敏感的营运资本痛点；但该验证目前仅有公司自述，尚无独立审计或第三方案例支撑。
zh.replaces: 传统 WMS/ERP 中人工维护的再订货点与 ABC 分类规则，以及依赖采购员经验逐品类判断补货量与安全库存的周期。
zh.segment: 中大型工业及商业零售的 SKU 级库存与补货决策，尤其是品类宽、供应商多、含阶梯价与最小起订量约束的场景。
zh.product: 核心产品 Q-Foundry 是一个在 250 万产品、15 亿数据点上预训练的需求预测基础模型（公司披露），可识别趋势、季节性、离群点，并纳入天气、节假日、搜索趋势等外部因子；其下游模块 Agent Q 将预测转化为带解释的自动补货建议，同时优化阶梯价、最小起订量、仓储成本等多因素，用户最终审批放行。公司强调该模型为欧洲自研、运行于德国维尔茨堡自有硬件，定位为数据主权产品。功能边界目前限于需求预测与补货建议，尚未披露是否覆盖采购合同谈判、供应商切换或跨仓库调拨。
zh.customer: 目标使用者为企业中负责库存与采购的运营或计划团队；付费方大概率是工厂、品牌商或大型贸易商的经营管理者。痛点频率为每日——每天需决定每个 SKU 是否补货、补多少，且错误判断直接转化为资金占用或缺货损失。官网未展示任何具名客户案例，采用证据缺失。
zh.workflow: 输入端仅需一次销售/出货数据导出，无需实施项目即可在约一周内生成首份预测（公司披露 PoC 周期约一个月且免费）。每日闭环为五步：当日库存与在途信息→Q-Foundry 输出未来数日需求与不确定性区间→Agent Q 结合可用率目标、交期、最小起订、包装与成本生成具体订单建议→货物按交期到达→当日实际销量结算或损失。用户可查看 Agent Q 的解释并一键批准或修改，80–90% 的决策自动化为公司披露目标而非已验证结果。
zh.business_model: PoC 阶段免费（公司披露），但正式生产环境的定价页、订阅结构或按 SKU 计费模式均未在官网公开。无法判断是 SaaS 订阅、按预测 SKU 数阶梯计费，还是含硬件部署的一次性授权；单位经济推断：若自有硬件推理成本显著高于云 API，毛利结构可能与纯软件 AI 公司不同，但目前无数据支撑，仅为条件式推断。
zh.traction: 公司披露 Q-Foundry 已预训练于 250 万产品与 15 亿数据点，但数据来源（自有历史、合作客户、公开数据集）未说明。官网无客户 logo 墙、无具名案例、无收入或 ARR 数据。当前可确认的牵引力仅为 Pre-Seed 融资本身及免费 PoC 获客漏斗的搭建，尚未有第三方验证的采用规模。
zh.moat: 相对通用大模型（GPT-4 类）做库存预测，SOLISTIQ 的差异化在于：(1) 领域预训练——15 亿库存相关数据点形成的 Q-Foundry 基础模型，对 SKU 级补货场景的适配深度；(2) 欧洲数据主权叙事，自有硬件部署，对合规敏感客户有吸引力；(3) 多因素联合优化（阶梯价、MOQ、仓储成本）而非单一预测精度。壁垒条件：若竞品能用通用模型加少量领域微调达到相近精度，且客户对数据驻留要求放松，护城河将收窄。
zh.funding_read: 本轮被公司标注为 Pre-Seed（官网），融资记录中轮次字段为 Other；投资方含个人天使（Kohrmann、Seelig、Metzger、Dubosq）与机构 Superangels、May Ventures，未见明确领投。资金用途未披露。该阶段说明团队已完成模型预训练与 PoC 流程设计，下一步里程碑大概率是首批付费客户签约与收入确认。
zh.risks: 1) 若 24% 降误差与 15–25% 降库存仅为特定数据条件下的结果，客户实际品类结构（高周转、长尾、强促销）差异可能导致 ROI 不达预期，免费 PoC 向付费转化率低。2) 库存优化赛道已有 Kinaxis、o9、Blue Yonder 及多家德国本土玩家（如 ALEAS、myinvenio），若 SOLISTIQ 仅以预测精度为卖点而无端到端工作流锁定，易被头部 WMS 供应商的 AI 模块以捆绑方式压制。
zh.takeaway: SOLISTIQ 把「基础模型 + 领域数据预训练」直接落到 SKU 级补货这一高频、可量化、ROI 易算的场景，并用免费 PoC（一周出结果）大幅降低决策门槛——对 AI 创业者而言，选一个每天发生、误差可立即用库存天数或缺货损失度量的任务，比追求通用智能更易证明价值。
zh.watch_next: 未来两个季度内是否出现 3 个以上具名付费客户及可引用的库存/缺货改善数据；Q-Foundry 是否开放 API 或嵌入现有 WMS 而非独立 SaaS；以及自有硬件推理的边际成本是否随 SKU 数线性增长，决定定价模型能否支撑毛利。

en.summary: SOLISTIQ builds Q-Foundry, a domain-specific foundation model for demand forecasting, and Agent Q, an explainable auto-replenishment layer, targeting industrial and commercial companies' SKU-level inventory and ordering decisions.
en.judgment: If the company-reported 24 % forecast-error reduction and 15–25 % inventory reduction hold in heterogeneous client portfolios, SOLISTIQ addresses a high-frequency, quantifiable pain point in working capital; however, both figures remain self-reported with no third-party audit or published case study to corroborate them.
en.replaces: Manual reorder-point and ABC-classification rules in legacy WMS/ERP, plus the purchasing-manager experience loop of judging order quantities and safety stock category by category.
en.segment: Mid-to-large manufacturing, branded-goods, and trading companies that manage wide SKU portfolios with tiered pricing, minimum-order-quantity constraints, and multi-supplier lead-time variability.
en.product: Q-Foundry is pre-trained on 2.5 million products and over 1.5 billion data points (company-reported); it captures trends, seasonality, and outliers, and ingests external signals such as weather, holidays, and search-trend data. Downstream, Agent Q converts forecasts into concrete order suggestions that jointly optimise tiered pricing, minimum quantities, storage costs, and availability targets, with a human-approval step. The model is developed in Germany and runs on SOLISTIQ's own hardware in Würzburg, positioned as an EU-sovereignty offering. Current scope ends at order recommendation; procurement contracting, supplier substitution, and cross-warehouse transfer are not documented.
en.customer: Day-to-day users are inventory-planning or purchasing teams inside a single enterprise; the economic buyer is likely an operations or finance director responsible for working capital. The pain recurs daily—every SKU requires a make/order/no-order decision, and a wrong call translates immediately into either stockout loss or excess carrying cost. No named customer logos or case studies appear on the site; adoption evidence is absent.
en.workflow: Onboarding requires a one-time export of sales/shipping data; no implementation project is needed. A free proof-of-concept (company-reported, ≈ 1 month) replays the client's last several months day-by-day: (1) stock and open deliveries at day t; (2) Q-Foundry outputs forecast and uncertainty band; (3) Agent Q factors availability target, lead time, MOQ, packaging, and cost to produce a specific order quantity; (4) goods arrive after lead time; (5) actual demand at day t either depletes stock or results in lost sales; the cycle repeats at t+1. The user reviews Agent Q's explanation and approves or overrides. 80–90 % automation is a company-stated target, not a measured figure.
en.business_model: The PoC is free (company-reported). Production pricing, subscription tiers, per-SKU billing, or hardware-licence structures are not published. Unit-economics inference is conditional: if inference runs on owned hardware at a marginal cost that scales linearly with SKU count, gross margin structure may differ from a pure cloud-AI SaaS; no data currently supports or refutes this.
en.traction: The only confirmed signal is the Pre-Seed financing itself and the funnel design around a free one-week PoC. The 2.5 M-product / 1.5 B-datapoint training corpus is company-reported; its provenance (proprietary, partner, public) is unstated. No revenue, ARR, client count, or third-party validation is available in the captured evidence.
en.moat: Versus generic LLMs applied to forecasting, SOLISTIQ's differentiation rests on (1) domain pre-training depth—1.5 B inventory-specific data points baked into Q-Foundry; (2) EU data-sovereignty positioning with on-premises hardware; (3) multi-factor joint optimisation (MOQ, tiered pricing, storage cost) rather than single-metric forecast accuracy. The moat is conditional: if a general model plus light fine-tuning achieves comparable precision and client data-residency requirements relax, the differentiation narrows quickly.
en.funding_read: The company labels the round Pre-Seed on its site; the funding record lists stage as 'Other.' Investors include individual angels (Kohrmann, Seelig, Metzger, Dubosq) and funds Superangels and May Ventures; no explicit lead is identified. Use of proceeds is undisclosed. The stage signals that model pre-training and PoC workflow are complete; the next milestone is almost certainly first paid-client contracts and revenue recognition.
en.risks: 1) If the 24 % error reduction and 15–25 % inventory reduction are achievable only in favourable data regimes, heterogeneous client portfolios with high-turnover, long-tail, or heavy-promotion SKUs may see materially lower ROI, depressing PoC-to-paid conversion. 2) Established players (Kinaxis, o9, Blue Yonder, and German-local tools such as ALEAS) bundle AI forecasting inside broader supply-chain suites; without end-to-end workflow lock-in, SOLISTIQ risks being commoditised as a forecasting API bolted on to incumbent WMS platforms.
en.takeaway: Picking a daily, high-frequency task whose error is immediately measurable in inventory days or stockout cost—then pairing a domain foundation model with a zero-friction free PoC (one-week result, no implementation project)—is a repeatable pattern for AI founders who need to prove value before asking for a long sales cycle.
en.watch_next: Whether 3+ named paid customers with citable inventory/stockout-improvement numbers appear within two quarters; whether Q-Foundry is exposed via API or embedded in existing WMS versus a standalone SaaS; and whether owned-hardware inference marginal cost scales linearly with SKU count, which will determine whether the pricing model can sustain gross margins.
